question: Does either of two independently identified 39-vertex induced catalog cores admit any labeled four-vertex completion to a (5,5)-Ramsey graph on 43 vertices?

scope.labeling_note: The 39 retained catalog vertices are relabeled increasingly as 0..38, and the four added vertices are 39..42. This is a complete labeled completion space for the fixed core, not a Hamming ball.

formula_definition.edge_variable_semantics: A true variable denotes an edge.
formula_definition.variable_order: First, for added vertices 39,40,41,42 in that order, their edges to core vertices 0..38 in increasing order; then added-added pairs (39,40),(39,41),(39,42),(40,41),(40,42),(41,42).
formula_definition.clause_order: For new-vertex counts 1..4, enumerate chosen added vertices lexicographically and chosen core vertices lexicographically; emit the clique-blocking negative clause first when applicable, then the independent-set-blocking positive clause.
formula_definition.completeness: The independently checked core has no fixed K5 or I5. Every remaining five-set contains 1..4 added vertices and receives exactly the applicable clique and/or independent-set blocking clause.

execution_rule: Before each target formula generation and again immediately before each solver launch, require at least 2432696320 available bytes on the filesystem containing certificates/.
Generate the deterministic CNF and metadata only after all pinned input and source hashes match this plan.
Independently reconstruct and compare every clause, its order, all bindings, and formula metadata before solving.
Launch the pinned streaming solver/checker pipeline only through the pinned file-size gate, imposing RLIMIT_FSIZE=134217728 bytes on the pipeline and every child process.
Run targets sequentially in the listed order; never run both proof-producing solver pipelines concurrently.
On SAT, independently replay the DIMACS model, reconstruct the complete graph, count every five-set, and require both the Python exhaustive verifier and compiled C++ bitset verifier to accept.
On UNSAT, require both drat-trim verification and exact decompressed LRAT replay through lrat-check; only CERTIFIED_UNSAT is a mathematical conclusion.
After CERTIFIED_UNSAT, compress the CNF and DRAT losslessly with pinned zstd, test both archives, verify decompressed hashes, and remove the uncompressed copies only after those checks pass.
On a file-size limit, timeout, storage-gate failure, proof-check failure, hash mismatch, or any other error, record no SAT/UNSAT conclusion and stop before the next target.

outcome_policy.SAT: A dual-verified reconstructed graph is a global order-43 (5,5)-Ramsey witness.
outcome_policy.CERTIFIED_UNSAT: Exclude only all four-vertex completions of this one labeled 39-vertex fixed core.
outcome_policy.TIMEOUT_OR_ERROR: Make no mathematical claim for the target.
outcome_policy.scope_warning: Even certified UNSAT for both fixed cores is not global order-43 nonexistence.
